trust_decision.summary: SQLite SQL command page decides whether a user-typed statement is ATTACH / VACUUM INTO by a leading-whitespace/comment/BOM regex, and refuses it before execution; a SQLite authorizer (PHP 8.0+ / PDO PHP 8.5+) denies ATTACH as a second layer. At the pinned commit both are ALREADY present, BOM included.

landing_point.why: The only ATTACH denylist in the tree; the summary names ATTACH + BOM bypass, which leads straight to the $space prefix regex at adminer/sql.inc.php:140.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: No vulnerable site exists at the pinned commit to dismiss: the BOM-aware check (adminer/sql.inc.php:140) and the ATTACH authorizer (adminer/drivers/sqlite.inc.php:116-120) are already in place.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Adminer itself must still ATTACH the selected database file in select_db() (authorizer whitelists it via $this->attaching), and VACUUM into the temp '' database must keep working; an over-broad block of ATTACH/VACUUM would break opening databases and the Vacuum button.

O6_input_shapes: unknown: fix diff contains no source change (fix.diff:15-24 is a version bump only); pinned tree already handles whitespace, /* */ comments, line comments and UTF-8 BOM prefixes (adminer/sql.inc.php:140)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Remove the BOM alternative from $space (i.e. revert the real fix) so a BOM-prefixed ATTACH/VACUUM INTO passes the denylist.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This is exactly the pre-6.1.1 state described by CHANGELOG.md:21; the comment 'BOM - SQLite skips it' shows it was added later.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Authorizer only installed when setAuthorizer exists (PHP 8.0+ / PDO PHP 8.5+); on older runtimes the regex at adminer/sql.inc.php:213 is the only defence.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Version-gated defence is a realistic, documented limitation (CHANGELOG.md:22); a planted variant could drop the authorizer in one of the two SqliteDb implementations (SQLite3 at :14 vs PDO at :76) — a second implementation at short distance.

O9_family: CWE-94 code injection via SQL statement denylist bypass (SQLite ATTACH writes a file that may be executed as PHP)

O10_build.toolchain: PHP 8.x with sqlite3 or pdo_sqlite extension; Playwright (Node) for the project's e2e tests
O10_build.project_tests: tests/sqlite.spec.js (Playwright e2e) and tests/sqlite.php; no test mentioning ATTACH or BOM found in tests/

j.j_sites_touched: none (fix commit changes only CHANGELOG.md, adminer/include/version.inc.php, docs/versions.csv)
j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Strip a leading BOM from the whole query once before the denylist regex, rather than allowing BOM anywhere in the leading-space pattern.
